metaDescription: Mineral owner near Faxon, Lycoming County? Core dry-gas Marcellus territory near Williamsport. We buy oil and gas interests — honest look, no pressure.
heroLead: Faxon sits just outside Williamsport in Lycoming County, in ground that's been part of the dry-gas Marcellus core since the play's earliest years.
intro: Faxon is a small unincorporated community near Williamsport, in Lycoming County — one of the most heavily developed dry-gas counties in the entire Marcellus play. Families with land here have often had a lease in place since the initial leasing rush, and many have years of royalty statements to look back on.
We buy mineral and royalty interests near Faxon, whether your interest is actively producing, leased and quiet, or a fractional share from family land.

sections.heading: Lycoming County's place in the dry-gas core
paragraphs: Lycoming County has been one of the most consistently developed dry-gas counties in the play, and Faxon-area acreage generally has real production history available to review rather than speculative undeveloped potential.

sections.heading: What years of statements tell us
paragraphs: A well with a decade or more of production history shows exactly how its decline curve has behaved, which gives a far more reliable basis for valuing an interest than a newer well still in its early flush period.

sections.heading: Our approach to your file
paragraphs: We review lease terms, production trend, and current activity nearby before naming a number, and explain what we found either way.
If you're not sure whether your interest is still active, that uncertainty alone is a good reason to have it reviewed rather than assumed.

faqs.question: Is Lycoming County a strong part of the Marcellus dry-gas play?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's been one of the most heavily and consistently developed dry-gas counties since the play's early years, which generally means more production history available to evaluate.

faqs.question: I have years of royalty statements for my Faxon-area interest. Does that help?
faqs.answer: Yes, a longer production history gives a much clearer picture of a well's actual decline behavior than newer wells with limited data, and we specifically ask for recent statements for this reason.

faqs.question: What if my Faxon-area lease is old and I'm not sure of the terms?
faqs.answer: We can pull the recorded lease through the Lycoming County Recorder of Deeds if you don't have your own copy, and review the actual terms before discussing a purchase.

faqs.question: How do I know which specific well my Faxon-area interest is tied to?
faqs.answer: Your division order or royalty statement should list the well name and API number, and if you don't have those, we can identify the well through Lycoming County lease and permit records.
